title: REPL and Save Workflow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Test lines in a mock Thonny REPL, copy the ones that work into the Editor, save them to the board as main.py or test.py, and power-cycle to see what runs by itself.

educational.topic: MicroPython REPL versus saved programs and the main.py boot convention
learningObjectives: Decide when to test an idea in the REPL and when to save it in a file
Move working REPL lines into the Editor and save them to the board
Predict what runs after a power cycle with main.py or test.py saved
Explain why REPL variables disappear when the board loses power
prerequisites: The REPL and uploading programs with Thonny (Chapter 3)
Flash memory versus RAM (Chapter 2: Storing Your Programs)

controls.label: >>> Shell line
controls.purpose: Type one line and press Enter

controls.label: Save to board
controls.purpose: Store the Editor in the Flash list

controls.label: Unplug and replug
controls.purpose: Power-cycle: clear RAM, then run main.py if present

simulationModel.modelType: Mock REPL and boot sequence for a MicroPython board
assumptions: The Shell understands print of a string, 3 + 4, 10 / 3, simple assignments, and speed * 2
At power-up the board runs only main.py
A saved program shows output only from print(); expressions run silently
limitations: Only a few kinds of lines are understood; other input returns NameError or SyntaxError
boot.py and running files manually from Thonny are not modeled

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided workflow with a visible checklist and prediction before power-cycling
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Mock IDE with Shell input, file save, and power-cycle
keyQuestions: Why does speed * 2 fail before you type speed = 50?
What happens to REPL variables when the board is unplugged?
Why does test.py not run by itself after a power cycle?
Why does 3 + 4 show 7 in the REPL but nothing when main.py runs?
commonMisconceptions: Code typed in the REPL is saved on the board
Any saved .py file runs at power-up
A saved program prints every result the way the REPL does
assessmentOpportunities: Written prediction of the Shell output after a power cycle
Challenge: test.py does not print; main.py prints Ready to roll!
Exit ticket listing the three steps from REPL test to auto-run
